l1: Is the issue with capturing an image, applying an image, or mounting/servicing an offline image?
What imaging format is in use — WIM, VHD/VHDX, or FFU?
What deployment tool is orchestrating imaging — MDT, SCCM/ConfigMgr, or manual DISM?
What is the exact DISM error code and operation that failed?
Is the reference image being maintained/updated in place (servicing an existing WIM) or rebuilt from scratch each time?
l2: Is the image multi-indexed (several editions in one WIM), and if so, which index is targeted?
Is the reference image fully generalized (sysprepped) before capture, or captured live?
Is servicing being done offline (mounted WIM) or online (running OS)?
Is the destination hardware using the same firmware type (UEFI vs legacy BIOS) and partition style (GPT vs MBR) as the reference image was built for?

l1: Run 'Dism /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:<path>.wim' to list all indexes and editions contained in the image.
Run 'Dism /Get-MountedWimInfo' to check for any images left mounted from a previous session.
Check %windir%\Logs\DISM\dism.log for the exact failing operation and error code.
Confirm free disk space on both the source and destination volumes before capture/apply.
l2: Run 'Dism /Image:<mount dir> /Get-Packages' or '/Get-Drivers' to inspect exactly what is present in an offline-mounted image.
Check whether an image is stuck mounted-but-invalid using 'Dism /Cleanup-Mountpoints' candidates before assuming corruption.
For capture issues, confirm whether the reference machine was booted into Windows PE/audit mode versus a live OOBE session, which affects what gets captured.
Cross-reference dism.log timestamps against imagex/DISM capture or apply command-line parameters used, to rule out a wrong index or wrong split-WIM (.swm) reference.

l1: Free up disk space on the source or destination and retry the capture/apply.
Unmount and discard a stuck offline image with 'Dism /Unmount-Image /MountDir:<dir> /Discard' before retrying.
Confirm the correct image index is specified with '/Index:' when applying a multi-edition WIM.
Verify the destination disk is partitioned correctly (UEFI/GPT vs BIOS/MBR) to match the image's boot requirements.
Run capture/apply operations from an elevated prompt — permission errors are a common, easily-missed cause of failed imaging operations.
If capturing to a network share, confirm the account running DISM/imagex has write access and the share has enough free space for the full WIM.
l2: For a corrupted mount, run 'Dism /Cleanup-Mountpoints' to clear orphaned mount points system-wide, then retry the operation from a clean state.
For servicing failures inside a mounted image, treat it like the Windows Servicing CBS/component-store troubleshooting flow, but scoped to the offline image path via '/Image:' instead of '/Online'.
If capture includes unwanted user/machine-specific state, re-capture only after a proper 'sysprep /generalize /oobe /shutdown' pass on the reference machine.
For apply failures on mismatched firmware/partition style, reformat the destination disk with the matching partition style (diskpart 'convert gpt' or 'convert mbr') before reapplying.

l1: Record the exact DISM error code and the operation (capture, apply, mount, commit) that failed.
Note the image format (WIM/VHDX/FFU) and whether it is multi-indexed.
Confirm the deployment tool in use (MDT, SCCM, manual DISM/imagex).
Note free disk space on both source and destination at the time of failure.
l2: Collect 'Dism /Get-ImageInfo' output for the image in question.
Collect 'Dism /Get-MountedWimInfo' output to check for orphaned/stuck mounts.
If a deployment tool orchestrated the task, collect its own task sequence/log output (e.g. SMSTS.log for SCCM, BDD.log for MDT) alongside dism.log.

image_stuck_mounted_and_wont_unmount.title: An offline WIM image is stuck mounted and won't cleanly unmount

steps.expect: Shows the image listed as mounted, possibly with an Invalid status
Either succeeds, or fails and confirms the mount point itself is corrupted

steps.action: Run 'Dism /Cleanup-Mountpoints' to clear all orphaned/corrupted mount points system-wide
steps.expect: Orphaned mounts are cleared and the mount registry is reset
No images remain mounted; the mount directory can be reused

apply_fails_firmware_partition_mismatch.title: Image apply fails due to firmware/partition style mismatch

steps.action: Check dism.log for a boot-configuration or partition-related failure during apply
steps.expect: Confirms the failure is tied to disk layout rather than the image content itself

steps.action: Compare the reference image's expected firmware type (UEFI/GPT vs legacy BIOS/MBR) against the destination disk's actual layout via diskpart
steps.expect: Confirms a mismatch, e.g. an MBR disk targeted for a UEFI-only image

steps.action: In diskpart, clean the destination disk and convert it to the matching style ('convert gpt' or 'convert mbr'), then recreate the required partitions
steps.expect: Destination disk layout now matches the image's boot requirements
Apply completes and the device boots successfully to OOBE

capture_fails_disk_space_or_permissions.title: Image capture fails partway through — disk space or permissions

steps.action: Check dism.log for the exact point of failure and whether it references disk space or access denied
steps.expect: Confirms whether this is a space or a permissions issue

steps.action: Confirm free space at the capture destination and the executing account's write permissions there
steps.expect: Identifies the specific missing resource or permission

steps.action: Free space or redirect the capture to a location with sufficient room, and/or grant the correct write permissions
steps.expect: Destination now has adequate space and correct permissions
Capture completes and produces a valid WIM file

answer_file_settings_not_applied_during_.title: Unattend.xml settings do not apply after an image is applied

steps.action: Confirm the answer file was actually referenced during apply (correct path passed to DISM/imaging tool) rather than assumed automatic
steps.expect: Confirms whether the file was even used in this operation

steps.action: Check setupact.log/setuperr.log for the specific configuration pass (specialize, oobeSystem, etc.) where the setting should have applied
steps.expect: Identifies which pass failed to process the intended setting

steps.action: Validate the answer file's XML against the correct component schema for this Windows build using Windows System Image Manager, and correct the misplaced or malformed setting
steps.expect: Answer file validates cleanly for the target build

steps.action: Reapply the image with the corrected answer file
steps.expect: Setting is present and correctly applied after OOBE
